files_reviewed: frontend/src/** (grep for setTimeout, console.log, TODO, toast, localStorage, NEXT_PUBLIC, localhost, innerHTML)
note: Both .env.example files were blocked by a permission rule and were not read. Storage is SQLite, so there is no row level security model and no database_rules labels. All model calls are server side (LangChain in backend/app/llm.py), so there are no ai_browser_call or secret_exposure labels. Real protections exist: refund approval queue with specialist approve and deny, ownership re-check in the action agent, webhook SSRF guard and HMAC signing, per-IP chat rate limit, CSV formula-injection guard, PII redaction before storage, regex prompt-injection guard, hash-chained audit log, CSRF header on cookie writes. Refund limit, return window, damaged item, missing package, carrier trace, fraud and safety escalations are enforced in code, not only in the prompt.

labels.what: The customer identity on /api/chat is the client-sent customer_id. _ensure_conversation (main.py 240-251) only checks that the customer exists, and context.py treats it as authenticated. Anyone can chat as any customer, see their orders and cancel or return them. The action agent ownership check (action_agent.py 35) compares against the same client value set at support_agent.py 228

The widget passes data-customer-id in the iframe URL (?customer=CUST-001) and the embed page uses it as the signed-in shopper. The comment says demo only, but there is no signed token path. widget-demo.html line 43 signs in as CUST-001

/api/demo/customers is public with no auth. It returns every customer's name, email, tier and order ids. That also gives an attacker the email needed for guest order verification (context.py 61-68). Docstring says remove in production

When no Google client id and no admin API key are set (the defaults in config.py 85 and 89), every console call returns Principal role admin. Approvals, exports, customer data export and erase, team management and settings are open to anyone
Conversation read, message poll and feedback routes have no auth and no ownership check. The conversation id is the only secret, so anyone holding an id reads the full transcript or rates it
Demo reset endpoint ships in the production API and needs only agent role. It deletes every row in the actions table and undoes all order cancellations, returns and refunds

The customer yes step that gates cancel and start_return is a loose regex. AFFIRMATIVE matches please or ok at the start, and it wins over NEGATIVE, so a reply like Please don't cancel or Ok wait, no executes the pending cancel

needs_approval gates only the refund type. cancel_order records a refund of the full order total with no amount check, so the 250 dollar approval limit is bypassed for cancels (demo order ORD-10460 is 299.23 and processing)

cancel_order, start_return and refund only write a JSON patch to the local order_state table. No payment provider, OMS or carrier is called, but the replies say the authorization is released and the refund is approved
start_return tells the customer a prepaid label was emailed to their address and returns a random RMA number. No email is sent and no label is created anywhere
Docstring says Mock commerce backend. Every customer and order lookup the agents use reads backend/data/*.json through an lru_cache. Production would need Shopify or an OMS

Five sample customer records (Maya Chen, Jordan Alvarez and others) with emails, phones, addresses, tiers and lifetime values, used as the real customer store. The backend Dockerfile copies data/ into the production image
Twelve sample orders with items, totals, tracking numbers and events, used as the real order store for lookups and actions
Seed script fills the console and analytics with scripted demo conversations, CSAT ratings and a backdated baseline week. It is a run-by-hand script
Landing page panel shows hardcoded knowledge gaps with ask counts under a Last 30 days label. Other panels are marked Sample data
TODAY is fixed to 2026-09-15 and drives return windows, delay detection and refund dates in actions. The real date is never used
The help article states the approval limit as 250 dollars, but refund_approval_limit is editable at runtime from Settings. A changed limit makes the AI quote a policy the code no longer applies
Return window 60 and 90 days and the 5.95 return fee are hardcoded in code and repeated as text in the knowledge base (lines 9 and 18). They are not in settings
SLA hours are hardcoded and the customer text says business hours and business days while the due time is computed in wall-clock hours
API URL falls back to http://localhost:8000. Docker-compose (lines 10 and 19), frontend/Dockerfile line 6 and config.py line 84 also default to localhost
Growth plan price 349 is hardcoded twice in the UI. The Start 14-day trial button only links to /demo. There is no billing or trial signup
The admin API key is saved in localStorage (relay.adminKey) and read by any script on the page
Copilot rewrite and KB draft endpoints call the paid model with no rate limit. In the default open mode anyone can call them
Prompt says warranty claim reviews and account recovery must go to a human. _policy_override (108-138) and the hard triggers have no rule for either, so the model alone decides
Prompt says never claim a refund, replacement, return or cancellation is done. The model's reply text is sent as-is with no output check
Prompt says never ask for full card numbers, passwords or 2FA codes. Redaction runs only on customer input. Nothing checks the model's reply
